fit-ann-arbor-art-fair.editorialNote: Read this row carefully: 'Ann Arbor Art Fair' is not one show. It is several independently juried fairs — the Street Art Fair (The Original), the Summer Art Fair, the State Street District fair and others — running concurrently across 30 blocks. The figures here are the combined event. You apply to a specific fair, each with its own jury, deadline and fee, and they are not equivalent in standing or in who walks past. Electricity is included in the booth fee, which is unusual at this scale.

juryOdds.basis: applying to several of the concurrent fairs materially improves the odds of being in Ann Arbor at all

logistics.basis: a 30-block downtown footprint; load-in depends heavily on which of the fairs you are in and where

powerAvailable.basis: electricity included in the booth fee

fit-art-in-the-high-desert.editorialNote: No commission and no Oregon sales tax, against all-corner booths. On a $10,000 weekend that is worth more than the entire booth fee. The jury is blind — images only, including a booth shot — so presentation carries real weight. Runs the last weekend of August; 2027 dates not yet published.

fit-kings-mountain-art-fair.editorialNote: The cheapest-looking entry on the circuit and, for expensive work, one of the dearest. $20 jury and $100 for the weekend, then 15% of everything you sell — $1,200 on a single $8,000 piece, against $600 for a booth at Art in the High Desert with no commission at all. For prints and small work the arithmetic reverses completely. Labor Day weekend, competing with Long's Park and (when it runs) Sausalito.

fit-sausalito-art-festival.editorialNote: CHECK BEFORE PLANNING A SEASON AROUND THIS ONE. The festival has been suspended over problems at its Marinship Park site, and the foundation has been running other events in its place. Its Labor Day slot is one of three strong competing dates, so if it is not running, Long's Park and Kings Mountain are the alternatives. Everything recorded here describes the show as it last ran, not a confirmed 2027 edition.

The scores on this row still describe the show as it was in Uptown; a move of that kind changes the crowd, the foot traffic and the character of the weekend, and none of that has been reassessed here. Treat the fit number as stale until members report back from the new site.
